title: Bounded scalar curvature and smooth extension of four-dimensional Ricci flow

issues.description: The decisive upper bound E = o(M) is imported wholesale from the companion paper StaticTrees (Thm 2.2). This paper does not prove it. The overall result is only as sound as that companion. A sibling review (rank 177) found no gap there, but it only skimmed the path-selection induction.
issues.evidence: Sec. 2: 'The remaining static proof, including path selection and the augmented elliptic construction, is supplied by the complete companion.' Prop. final:functional-smallness relies on it for every extracted tree.

issues.location: Sec. 4 (Thm 4.1 degeneration, Prop. root-scale, Lemma geodesic-radius, Vol{l<s}<=Cs^4)
issues.description: The geometric inputs are mostly Bamler–Zhang-type facts that the paper sketches or re-derives: genuine orbifold points, finite trees, uniform exterior charts with error Θ(r), and curvature radius along minimizing segments. I only skimmed them and did not verify them in detail. They look plausible and agree with known 4D results.
issues.evidence: Section 4 is 1432 lines; I checked only how its statements are used in Sections 5 and 7.

coverage: Read Sections 1, 2, 5 and 7 in full, the statement and setup of Section 6, and the theorem statements of Section 4. Checks made: first-variation sign ⟨½Rg−Ric, −2Ric⟩ = 2|Ric|²−R²; the functional scaling and |E| ≤ CM lemma, including the child-half exponent computation; the tail-variation scaling b⁴(a/b)^{4+2α} = a⁴N^{-2α}; the IBP plus Cauchy–Schwarz closure using the Hardy–Littlewood maximal bound, giving K² ≤ γ(K+1)² and then K → 0; dimensional consistency of H_*, M and E between root and interval units; the radial operator L, with homogeneous exponents 1 and −3 and the values L(B^{-2}) and L(s^{-2}); the neck barrier and the positivity of the four decay exponents; the H-ratio bounds H^{-1+α} in the exterior recurrence; the distance-variation integral ∫ l^{-2} and the dyadic sum ∫ a/l ≤ Ca⁴; time-scale consistency (|Ric| ≤ C/l gives distance change at O(log) rate, so a scale change needs physical time ≫ a²). Not verified: the full Section 4 geometry, the internals of the Section 6 collar-extension proof (Korn and Newton estimates), and the companion static theorem.
main_claim: A smooth Ricci flow on a closed 4-manifold with uniformly bounded scalar curvature on [0,T), T<∞, extends smoothly past T on the same manifold. Equivalently, scalar curvature blows up at any finite-time singularity in dimension 4.
sibling_notes: Family 351 also contains the companion 'Path-selection-and-an-elliptic-inequality-on-degenerating-Ricci-flat-trees' (rank 177, no_gap_found, path-selection induction only skimmed). This paper's Thm 2.2 is exactly that companion's main static inequality E = o(M), so a gap there would propagate here directly.
